claim: test_schema_loading.md:280-286 (IH6, 'Empty parts and empty input') requires that IdentityHash(), IdentityHash(""), and IdentityHash("a", "", "b") produce three mutually distinct hashes, and its Verifies line states the function 'does not silently treat empty strings as identical to absent parts.'
authoritative_source: arch_schema_loader.md:18-22 fixes the algorithm as `identity = join(parts, "/")` followed by SHA-256 and hex-truncation, with no special-casing for empty parts or a zero-length part list.
evidence: Under the join(parts, "/") algorithm arch_schema_loader.md declares, joining zero parts and joining a single empty-string part both yield the identity string "" (Go's strings.Join behaves this way, and any straightforward join implementation does too), so IdentityHash() and IdentityHash("") necessarily hash the same input and produce the same output. IH6's requirement that all three calls be pairwise distinct is unsatisfiable against the declared algorithm without changing it — e.g. join(parts, "/") does not encode the distinction between "no parts" and "one empty part", the same way join(["a",""], "/") = "a/" collides with join(["a"], "/") in a different degenerate case that IH6 does not test but the same defect covers. The two leaves disagree on whether that collision is acceptable: test_schema_loading.md's Verifies line explicitly forbids it, arch_schema_loader.md's algorithm guarantees it.
proposed_fix: Either (a) relax IH6 to assert only totality and pattern-conformance on degenerate input, dropping the h1-distinct-from-h2 requirement, matching the join(parts, "/") algorithm as declared, or (b) amend the algorithm in arch_schema_loader.md to make empty-vs-absent distinguishable (e.g. join on a separator that cannot appear in a part list of a different shape, or prefix the identity string with the part count) and update every worked example in the same leaf accordingly. Advisory only — the authoring loop decides.
